summary: array-native-utils ships an encrypted dropper that stages and executes an opaque payload on require()
details: The package is advertised as lightweight array utilities (flatten/compact/unique) but index.js top-level require loads a platform-specific.node binary that acts as a dropper. The native binaries locate an adjacent 10.9 MB high-entropy file named.napi_cache (no printable strings, consistent with an encrypted/packed blob), stage it to /tmp/.<pid> on Linux/macOS or %TEMP%\...nc%lu.js on Windows, set executable/hidden attributes, and spawn it as a detached child via fork+setsid+execlp or CreateProcessA with 'node "%s"'. The JavaScript surface area (array utilities) is pure JS and has no legitimate need for a native addon, confirming the native module is pretext. Before firing, the binaries check an extensive list of CI/build and analysis indicators — GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, /proc/1/cgroup, containerd, dockerinit, /proc/self/status TracerPid, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, wireshark — to avoid executing in sandboxes, build farms, and researcher environments and run only on real developer or production hosts. Any process that requires this package outside such a gated environment will decrypt and execute attacker-controlled code with the privileges of the host process.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
